---
title: "Growing a vector in a loop gets more and more expensive"
ref: DF-08
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "`FALSE`: four times as many iterations, roughly four times the time"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
grow <- function(n) {
  x <- c()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    x <- c(x, i^2)
  }
  x
}
t_small <- system.time(grow(5000))[["elapsed"]]
t_large <- system.time(grow(20000))[["elapsed"]]
t_large > 4 * t_small
```
:::

## Why

`x <- c(x, i^2)` does not add a slot at the end of `x`: it creates a new vector, copies the whole old one into it, then appends the value. Iteration number 10,000 copies 10,000 numbers. The total work grows as the square of `n`: four times as many iterations take roughly sixteen times as long, hence the `TRUE`.

The trap is the same with `rbind()` in a loop to stack data.frames, and even slower, since each added row copies the whole table.

## The remedy

Reserve the space once and for all, then fill it. Better still, when possible, compute in one go on the whole vector, and for data.frames, stack only once at the end.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
preallocate <- function(n) {
  x <- numeric(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    x[i] <- i^2
  }
  x
}
identical(preallocate(20000), y = grow(20000))
identical(preallocate(20000), y = seq_len(20000)^2)

pieces <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  data.frame(i = i, square = i^2)
})
do.call(rbind, pieces)
```
:::
